tools.name: thread_state_get
tools.summary: Read what this agent saved about the person it is talking to.
tools.when_to_use: At the start of a turn that continues earlier work with this person: the step reached, the data already collected, a choice they made.
limits: One record per person: every call works on the record of whoever sent the current message, shared by all their conversations with this agent. `state_key` is required, but it does not choose the record.
Only this agent sees the record: it is kept on its node's disk.
tools.present_when: the message names its sender (`src_ilk`), and the node's state store opened at start

state_key.description: Any non-empty label. The record is always the sender's.

output.description: `{found: true, state_key, data, updated_at, ttl_seconds}` with the saved record, or `{found: false, state_key}` when there is none.

state_key.description: The record's key: the sender's ILK.

ttl_seconds.description: The ttl_seconds of the last put. Nothing expires the record.

tools.name: thread_state_put
tools.summary: Save what this agent needs to remember about the person it is talking to.
tools.when_to_use: As soon as something worth keeping changes (a step reached, data collected, a decision), before you answer.
limits: One record per person: every call works on the record of whoever sent the current message, shared by all their conversations with this agent. `state_key` is required, but it does not choose the record.
A put replaces the whole record: keep everything in one object. Read it with `thread_state_get`, change it, and put all of it back.
Only this agent sees the record: it is kept on its node's disk.
`ttl_seconds` is stored with the record, but nothing expires it.
tools.present_when: the message names its sender (`src_ilk`), and the node's state store opened at start

data.description: What to keep, as one JSON value: it replaces the record.

state_key.description: Any non-empty label. The record is always the sender's.

ttl_seconds.description: Kept with the record and returned by `thread_state_get`; nothing expires it.

output.description: `{ok: true, state_key}` once the record is saved.

state_key.description: The record's key: the sender's ILK.

tools.name: thread_state_delete
tools.summary: Delete what this agent saved about the person it is talking to.
tools.when_to_use: When the work with this person is over and nothing should carry into their next conversation, or when they ask you to forget it.
limits: It deletes the record of whoever sent the current message, whatever `state_key` says.
Deleting a record that does not exist succeeds.
tools.present_when: the message names its sender (`src_ilk`), and the node's state store opened at start

state_key.description: Any non-empty label. The record is always the sender's.

output.description: `{ok: true, state_key}` once the record is gone.

state_key.description: The record's key: the sender's ILK.

tools.name: generate_csv_artifact
tools.summary: Make a CSV file from rows of text and send it to the user.
tools.when_to_use: When the user wants a table as a file, to open in a spreadsheet or another program.
limits: Every cell is written quoted. A cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return, or with `-` and is not a plain number such as `-12.5`, gets a `'` in front, so a spreadsheet takes it as text, never as a formula.
`headers`, when given, is the first row.

Your reply is the text you write after your last tool call; text written alongside a call is not sent. Every file this reply's calls make goes with it, in order, up to 8: a call past that makes none, and a file with an earlier one's name takes its place. You get back the file's name, type and size, never its content.

filename.description: The file's name, as the user sees it: it ends in .csv, with at most 128 bytes and no `/`, `\`, `..` or control character.

rows.description: The rows, each a list of cells.

output.description: `{status: "ok", filename, mime, size_bytes}`: the file is kept for your reply.

errors.meaning: `filename` is empty, longer than 128 bytes, has `/`, `\`, `..` or a control character, or does not end in .csv. No file was made.
The reply already carries 8 files, the most one reply can. No file was made: say so in your reply, and make the rest in a later one.

tools.name: get_current_time
tools.summary: Get the current date and time, in UTC and in a time zone.
tools.when_to_use: Whenever the answer depends on today's date or the time of day: what day it is, how long until a date, whether something is due or open now. You do not know the date: never guess it.
limits: `timezone` is an IANA zone name, such as `America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires` or `Europe/Madrid`; without it, UTC. Use the user's zone when you know it.
It only reads the time: it cannot schedule anything or wait.
tools.present_when: always: SY.timer of the agent's hive answers it, and SY.timer runs on the motherbee and on every worker

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name, such as America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires. UTC when absent.

output.description: `{status: "ok", utc, local, timezone, abbreviation, weekday}`: the time in UTC and in the zone (ISO 8601, to the millisecond; the local one with its offset), the zone and its abbreviation, and the local weekday in English.

abbreviation.description: The zone's abbreviation at that moment, such as CET or -03.

local.description: In the zone, with its offset, such as 2026-10-27T12:04:05.123-03:00.

weekday.description: The weekday of the local date, Monday to Sunday.

errors.meaning: `timezone` is not an IANA time zone name. Call again with one, or without it for UTC.
SY.timer did not answer: the agent's hive does not run it, or it is restarting. `retryable: true`: try once more shortly, and never guess the time.

tools.name: read_blob
tools.summary: Read a text file from this hive's blob store, by its blob name.
tools.when_to_use: When an attachment's text was cut, or you need an attached text file again: every attachment shows its blob name, `<name>_<hash16>.<ext>`, and a cut one also the offset to read on from. Read a long file a piece at a time.
limits: A text file (csv, json, md, html, txt, logs…), judged by its content, whatever its name: a piece with a NUL byte, as binary files have, is `not_text`. Bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD, as in an attachment.
Files up to 10 MiB. Each call returns up to 64 KiB of text from `offset`, in bytes of the text, cut where a character starts; read on from `next_offset`.
Up to 192 KiB of text in all for one message, over all its calls.
It waits up to 20 s for a blob still on its way from another hive.
tools.present_when: always: every hive with agents has a blob store

blob_name.description: The blob's name, `<name>_<hash16>.<ext>`, as an attachment shows it.

offset.description: Where to start, in bytes of the text: 0 by default, the `next_offset` of the piece before, or the offset a cut attachment gives.

output.description: `{status: "ok", blob_name, size_bytes, offset, text, next_offset}`: the text from `offset`, the whole text's size in bytes, and where the next piece starts (null at the end).

next_offset.description: Where the next piece starts; null at the end.

offset.description: Where `text` starts, in bytes: the offset asked for, moved back to the start of a character.

size_bytes.description: The whole text's size, in bytes: the file's, when it is UTF-8.

errors.meaning: `blob_name` is not a blob's name, `<name>_<hash16>.<ext>`: use the name an attachment shows, whole.
The piece read has a NUL byte: the file is binary, not text. It cannot be read.
No blob of this hive has that name, after waiting 20 s for one on its way, or what is there is not that blob.
The file is over 10 MiB, the most it reads.
This message has read 192 KiB of blob text, the most one message reads. Not retryable within this message: answer with what you have read; a later message can read on.

tools.name: publish_html_page
tools.summary: Publish an HTML page at a public link, and get the link.
tools.when_to_use: Only when the user asks for a page to open or share by link. To hand over a file instead, use `generate_html_artifact`.
limits: One self-contained HTML file, served under a sandbox: its inline scripts and styles run, but it loads nothing from the network (no fetch, no outside scripts, stylesheets, fonts or images); images and fonts only inline, as `data:` URLs; forms do not submit.
The link is the key: anyone who has it can open the page, so put nothing private in it. It expires 24 hours after publishing, and you cannot extend it; `unpublish_html_page` takes it down sooner.

Publishing takes up to two minutes. Your reply is the text you write after your last tool call; text written alongside a call is not sent. Give the link there: a reply without it gets it added, on a line of its own.
tools.present_when: the node has its identity: it was launched with its ILK

filename.description: The page's file name: it ends in .html or .htm, with at most 128 bytes and no `/`, `\`, `..` or control character.

output.description: `{status: "ok", url, publication_id, expires_at}`: the public link, the publication's id and when it expires (Unix seconds).

errors.meaning: `filename` is empty, longer than 128 bytes, has `/`, `\`, `..` or a control character, or does not end in .html or .htm. Nothing was published.

The page was not published; `message` says why. `retryable: true` when this node's blob store or SY.admin could not be reached; `false` when SY.admin refused it (the message carries its code, such as BLOB_TOO_LARGE) or the hive has no public address for links.

tools.name: unpublish_html_page
tools.summary: Take down a page you published with `publish_html_page`, before it expires.
tools.when_to_use: When the user asks to take a page down, or a page you published is wrong: publish the right one and take the old one down. Name it by the link the user has, or by its publication_id.
limits: Only pages this agent published. Give exactly one of `url` or `publication_id`.
Taking a page down twice is harmless: a page already down, or expired, answers `unpublished: false`.
tools.present_when: the node has its identity: it was launched with its ILK

publication_id.description: The page's publication_id, `pub:<uuid>`, as `publish_html_page` gave it.

url.description: The page's link, as `publish_html_page` gave it: https://<host>/public/<key>, the key 64 lowercase hex characters.

output.description: `{status: "ok", publication_id, unpublished}`: `unpublished` is false when the page was already down or had expired.

errors.meaning: No page was published with that link or publication_id, or it is not one: a link's key is 64 lowercase hex characters after `/public/`.
Another node published that page: an agent takes down only its own.
SY.admin could not take the page down now. `retryable: true`: try again shortly; taking it down twice is harmless.
